description: Where a project keeps the things it cannot hold in source. Two failures live here and they point opposite ways: a variable the code needs and the environment does not have, and a secret the environment has and the browser can read.

gates.title: Every Variable The Code Reads Exists In Every Environment
gates.rule: Each variable named in source is set for development, preview and production. A variable present in production and missing in preview turns every branch deployment into a broken one, and the failure looks like the branch rather than the setting.
gates.fix: Add the missing variables per environment, then probe again. Anything genuinely local-only is named in the note.

gates.title: No Secret Sits Behind A Public Prefix
gates.rule: Nothing secret is named VITE_ or NEXT_PUBLIC_. Those prefixes are an instruction to the bundler to inline the value into the client, so the prefix does not protect the value, it publishes it.
gates.fix: Rename the variable without the prefix and read it server-side, or replace it with a key that is meant to be public.

gates.title: No Key Shape Survives Into The Built Client Bundle
gates.rule: The built output carries no service role key, no secret key and no private key. This is checked against the build rather than the source, because a value can reach the bundle through a re-export, a config object or a logging line that reads nothing like a leak.
gates.fix: Build, find which module pulled the value in, and move that work to the server. Rotate anything that has already shipped.

gates.title: env.example Lists Every Variable And No Value
gates.rule: The example file names every variable the code reads and carries none of their values. It is the only description of what a fresh clone needs, and a stale one turns a five-minute setup into an afternoon of guessing.
gates.fix: Regenerate it from what the source references, with empty values.

gates.title: Nothing Real Is Committed
gates.rule: No .env file holding real values is tracked by git, and none appears in the history. A secret removed in a later commit is still published; the fix is rotation, not deletion.
gates.fix: Untrack the file, add it to .gitignore, and rotate every value it carried.

gates.title: Every Secret Has A Copy In CryptoFort
gates.rule: Each secret this project depends on is stored in the vault, so an environment that has to be rebuilt can be. A value that exists only in a Vercel settings page is a value one deleted project away from being gone.
gates.fix: credential_put each one, then name in the note which credentials were filed and under what names. Never paste a value into the note.
